reason: The contract requires componentwise |actual-target| <= 1e-7 + 5e-7*|target| over all finite FP16 component combinations including extrema, subnormals, and signed zeros, plus all-finite outputs. All three in-scope failure hypotheses were tested with adversarial inputs and rebutted: (c1) cancellation rows with components at ±65504 produced zero tolerance violations (max err/tol ratio ~2e-5) because FP16×FP16 products are exactly representable in FP32 (11-bit mantissas, 24-bit FP32 mantissa), so numerators cancel exactly; (c2) non-cancelling extreme/subnormal-mixed rows produced zero violations (max err/tol ratio 1.9e-4), since only the scale sum and final div_rn round, adding ≤~1.5 ulp relative error against the 5e-7 budget; (c3) exhaustive combinations of ±65504, ±6e-8, ±0.0, 1.0 (6241 legal rows) produced zero non-finite outputs, as intermediates ≤8.6e9 cannot overflow FP32. The artifact has no test.py/get_inputs narrowing the domain, so problem.txt is the operative contract and the adversarial probes directly cover the domain clauses it requires. Skeptic reviewed the latest evidence and recorded no new claims; no open claims remain. Signed-zero differences are acceptable under the contract's "signed zeros are numerically equal" clause. Evidence is decisive for trust.
